name: preCICE
listed_description: Coupling library for partitioned multi-physics simulations (FSI, CHT, and more).
reason: No numeric comparison against a named baseline in anything reachable. Opened the repo page (no performance text) and the benchmarks/ directory: Google Benchmark microbenchmarks (mesh index, mesh tagging, RBF assembly kernels, write-data, bounding box, profiling) that time preCICE internals only, with no external library or older version as baseline. Leads not reachable (hosts EGRESS_BLOCKED): STFC report Rubin, 'Comparison of code coupling libraries for high performance multi-physics simulation', DL-TR-2022-001, DOI 10.5286/dltr.2022001 (MUI, MOOSE, preCICE, OpenPALM, PLE on a 3D field exchange; epubs.stfc.ac.uk/work/52144823); arXiv 2512.10724 (preCICE 3.3.0 on an Earth System Model regridding benchmark) compares accuracy, not runtime, and says a runtime comparison to ESM couplers is out of scope. The preCICE developer claim that MpCCI's central coupling server limits performance has no numbers.

name: Project Chrono
listed_description: An open source multi-physics simulation engine.
reason: No numeric comparison against a named baseline reachable. README has no performance claims. Chrono issue #147 (a request to add Chrono to the SimBenchmark of RaiSim, Bullet, ODE, MuJoCo and DART): maintainers postponed benchmarking in 2019, closed 2026-03-10 with no results. Lead not reachable (ideas.repec.org, copernicus and dtic hosts blocked): Pazouki, Mazhar and Negrut, 'Parallel collision detection of ellipsoids with applications in large scale multibody dynamics', Math. Comput. Simul. 82(5):879-894, 2012, whose abstract (seen in a search summary only) reports a 14-fold speedup of GPU ellipsoid contact detection over CPU sphere contact detection in Bullet; that is a GPU-vs-CPU, ellipsoid-vs-sphere comparison and was not tied to the current Chrono code, so no record was written.

name: Reaktoro
listed_description: A computational framework in C++ and Python for modeling chemically reactive systems.
reason: No numeric comparison against a recognizable external baseline reachable. README and repo page carry no benchmark text (PHREEQC appears only as a supported database format) and the project documentation site is blocked. Lead not reachable (arxiv and ar5iv blocked): Kyas, Leal and coauthors, 'Accelerated reactive transport simulations in heterogeneous porous media using Reaktoro and Firedrake', arXiv 2009.01194, whose on-demand machine learning algorithm is reported (search summary only) to make equilibrium calculations one to three orders of magnitude faster; its baseline is Reaktoro's own conventional Gibbs energy minimization, not PHREEQC, GEMS or another solver, so it does not qualify as a comparison with another solver.

name: Recommender
listed_description: C library for product recommendations/suggestions using collaborative filtering (CF).
reason: Only absolute numbers and no named baseline: the README says 'Fast running time ~ 81 seconds for 10 million ratings (on MovieLens Data Sets)' and 'Memory footprint under 160 MB for 10 million ratings', with no hardware, compiler flags or comparison library. Repo page, issues list (4 issues, none about comparisons) and tools/ folder (kfold, serialization, shuffle) opened; nothing compares against Mahout, LensKit, Surprise, TensorFlow or any other library. The project page on github.io is blocked.

name: QuarkPhysics
listed_description: A 2D Soft Body and Rigid Body Physics Engine.
reason: No numbers and no baseline: the README and repo page only list features ('Supports sleeping islands to improve CPU performance', roadmap items 'Optimizations' and 'Multithreading') and contain no benchmark or comparison with Box2D, Chipmunk, Bullet or ODE.
